uncited: Lighting and Shading Models compute the color of a surface point identified by distance-field ray marching by combining geometric properties (normals, depth) with light source parameters.
This family solves the problem of transforming raw geometric hits into visually plausible images by simulating how light interacts with surfaces.

It is distinct from [Distance-field ray marching](21-distance-field-ray-marching.md) (which finds *where* the surface is) and [Volumetric and Atmospheric Rendering](4968-volumetric-and-atmospheric-rendering.md) (which computes light transport *through* participating media), focusing instead on surface reflectance and local illumination effects [S5, S7, S10, unofficial].
All methods in this family operate on a surface point $\mathbf{p}$ and its associated geometric data, primarily the surface normal $\mathbf{n}$.
**Geometric Setup:** Determine the view direction $\mathbf{v}$ (from $\mathbf{p}$ to camera) and light direction $\mathbf{l}$ (from $\mathbf{p}$ to light source) [S7, S10, unofficial].

**Occlusion/Ambient Occlusion:** Calculate shadow factors or ambient occlusion values to determine how much light reaches $\mathbf{p}$ from the environment or specific lights [S3, S4, S5, S10, unofficial].
**Color Accumulation:** Combine the base material color with the lighting contributions, often modulated by depth cueing or atmospheric effects [S5, S7, unofficial].
